name: gameplay-candy-belt
origin: The Candy Factory belt carrying what the candy machine makes (checkpoint 5, feature motion), on the round of gameplay-candy-start (seed 42, Arcade, Normal, robot 0; the AI robots stopped at the round's first frame, the player idle): ConveyorBelt.runEngine makes an item at the exit (8,9) every 210 ticks and moves everything on the track 1 px per tick (bombMove, propMove: xPos += offset, then resetDisplay). Captures: the first item, a bomb, 15 ticks out of the exit (bomb-out); a pickup made at tick 1260 sliding down from the exit (pickup-out) while a carried bomb leaves the belt's last cell (6,11) with Art_Prop_Disappear (bomb-gone: ConveyorBelt.addDisappearAni, frame 11); a pickup on the last straight (pickup-end), the same pickup gone with its Art_Prop_Disappear at frame 3 (pickup-gone) and at frame 16 (gone-late).
godot_note: Godot starts on the recorded round with the original's Math.random place (tests/goldens/gameplay-candy-start/math_random.json); a carried bomb or pickup is one view from cell to cell (scripts/ui/game_actors.gd). Its Date seconds follow the frames (--frame-clock): the case runs 49 s of round time, and ArcadeMode.timePassed's first timed pickup comes at 60 s, so neither side makes one.

actions.godot_note: The round this START opens takes its board and enemy robots from the golden of the candy-start capture (App.round_as_recorded), as gameplay-cinema-start does.
AIControl.stop through the original's own method (fixture); Godot gives the robot no commands, as it then has none.
